item.title: Effective Cache Busting Strategies for Web Assets: Query String vs. Filename Versioning
item.description:
“Effective Cache Busting Strategies for Web Assets: Query String vs. Filename Versioning”

When deploying updates to static assets like CSS or JavaScript files, forcing clients to fetch the new versions instead of relying on stale cached copies is critical. How should developers reliably implement cache busting? This discussion examines using query parameters versus modifying filenames, and the potential pitfalls associated with each technique, particularly concerning intermediary caches.

Is Using a Query Parameter for Versioning Effective for Cache Busting?

Leveraging a query string parameter, such as appending ?v=1.123 to a resource URL, serves to inform the browser that the resource has potentially changed from a previous version (e.g., ?v=1.0).
